evidence: src/presentation/web/TicketController.ts, TicketController.buy: `if (body.seats < 1 || body.seats > 8) { throw new TicketRejected('Between 1 and 8 seats per purchase'); }` enforces a business purchase-limit rule (domain responsibility)
The guard throws TicketRejected, which is imported from '../../business/core/TicketingError'. Using a domain error type shows this is domain policy, not request-format validation.
The rest of the class is appropriate presentation work: scan() and events() delegate to business services and format output with euros().
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of TicketController does normal presentation work. It defines request body shapes, hands work to the BoxOffice and GateLog business services, and formats money for the response with euros(). The exception is TicketController.buy, which enforces the purchase policy itself: a purchase must be for between 1 and 8 seats. The guard throws the domain error TicketRejected. This is not a check on the request's format. It is a business rule about how many tickets one purchase may include, so it belongs in the domain layer (for example BoxOffice.purchase). With the rule in the controller, any other caller of BoxOffice.purchase can skip it, and the business layer is no longer the single source of ticketing policy.
